row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following best explains the observed mediastinal shift and reduced right lung volume in the patient? 
A) Right pneumothorax causing collapse of the right lung.
B) Right pulmonary artery agenesis leading to reduced lung volume and compensatory hyperinflation of the left lung.
C) Right lung mass causing tracheal deviation and volume loss.
D) Right pleural effusion causing mediastinal shift and reduced lung volume.
E) Right lower lobe pneumonia causing volume loss and mediastinal shift.
F) Bilateral pulmonary embolism affecting the right lung more severely.

reference.correct_choice_text: Right pulmonary artery agenesis leading to reduced lung volume and compensatory hyperinflation of the left lung.

historical_prediction.json.raw_response:
Answer: B) Right pulmonary artery agenesis leading to reduced lung volume and compensatory hyperinflation of the left lung.  
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows mediastinal shift to the right and reduced right lung volume with increased lucency on the left, suggesting hypoplasia of the right lung. CT images (Figures 2a and 3b) confirm absence of the right pulmonary artery (arrow in Figure 3b), a hallmark of pulmonary artery agenesis, which causes ipsilateral lung hypoplasia and contralateral compensatory hyperinflation—consistent with the findings.

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When unilateral hyperlucency is present without obvious pleural line or mediastinal shift, and lung size appears reduced
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect ipsilateral intercostal space width and hemidiaphragm position relative to contralateral side; reduced spacing + elevated diaphragm supports volume loss (e.g., Swyer-James), not hyperinflation or pneumothorax
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Unreliable if inspiration inadequate or diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires comparison to contralateral side

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When unilateral hemithorax opacity with mediastinal shift lacks volume loss signs (normal diaphragm level, normal rib spacing) and bronchovascular markings are completely absent
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for congenital absence: confirm absence of right main bronchus on CT or bronchoscopy; consider agenesis over atelectasis
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Rare in elderly; requires cross-sectional imaging for confirmation; cannot be diagnosed by CXR alone
